reports.title: ESCO REPORTS FOURTH QUARTER AND FISCAL 2026 RESULTS

guidance.heading: Business Outlook – FY 2027
section: Expectations for growth in FY 2027 compared to FY 2026:

· | Net sales are expected to grow 55 to 58 percent to a range of $2.05 to $2.09 billion on a consolidated basis, with A&D growing 7 to 9 percent, USG growing 170 to 175 percent (7 to 9 percent organic growth plus Megger revenue of $640 to $660 million), and Test growing 5 to 7 percent.
· | Adjusted EBIT is expected to increase approximately 51 to 55 percent with Adjusted EBIT margins of 21.2 to 21.8 percent of sales.
· | Adjusted EBITDA is expected to increase approximately 53 to 57 percent with Adjusted EBITDA margins of 24.2 to 24.8 percent of sales.
· | Interest is expected to be in the range of $61 to $63 million in FY 2027.
· | The effective income tax rate is expected to be approximately 22.5 percent in FY 2027.
· | FY 2027 Adjusted EPS is expected to increase 12 to 15 percent to a range of $9.40 to $9.70 per share.
· | Q1 2027 Adjusted EPS is expected to increase 13 to 19 percent compared to Q1 2026 and be in the range of $1.85 - $1.95 per share.
· | Consistent with prior years, revenues and Adjusted EPS are expected to grow sequentially throughout the year.

desk.headline: Sales up 9% to $384m and adjusted EPS $2.67, both beat; FY27 guide of $2.05-2.09bn sales and $9.40-9.70 EPS includes Megger
results: Q4 sales rose 9% to $384m, all organic, and adjusted EPS rose 15% to $2.67; both beat estimates.
Aerospace & Defense led with sales up 12% on Navy and commercial aerospace; Test grew 11%; Utility (USG) grew 3% as renewables at NRG fell 20%.
Orders rose 22% in the quarter, and the year ended with a record $1.55bn backlog.
For the full year, sales grew 21% to $1.32bn and adjusted EPS 40% to $8.42.
The Megger acquisition closed on 1 October 2026, after year end.

guidance.summary: For fiscal 2027, including Megger, ESCO expects sales of $2.05-2.09bn (up 55%-58%) and adjusted EPS of $9.40-9.70 (up 12%-15%). Q1 adjusted EPS is guided at $1.85-1.95.

points: Management said it is highly confident of $20m of Megger cost savings in year one; no extra sales from the deal are assumed.
Navy demand stayed strong, with Navy sales up 18% and Navy backlog above $770m.
Weakness at NRG (renewables) and higher costs for electronic parts, steel and copper weighed on Utility margins.
The company had no net debt before funding Megger; cash flow is expected to be lower in 2027 as Navy advance payments ease.
Megger integration costs of about $30m are excluded from adjusted guidance.
